newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK STOCKS CLOSE LOWER AFTER TRADING NARROWLY.
newsitem.headline: GREEK STOCKS CLOSE LOWER AFTER TRADING NARROWLY.

text.p: The Athens bourse closed lower on thin volume as brokerages have become more cautious after the Delta Securities scandal and the investment public abstains, fund managers said.
The benchmank index closed at 905.65, 0.41 percent lower than the 909.34 close of Wendsday's session. Turnover was at4.095 billion drachmas on volume of 1.99 million shares.

"There seems to be no activity on behalf of institutional and individual investors," Alpha Mutual Funds' Manager Michalis Eleftheriou, said. "Securities companies have become more cautious after Delta Securities scandal. I do not see the stock market recovering in the very short-term."
On the Greek farmers' front, tension seems to be somewhat receding and farmers let some trapped foreign trucks pass through, ANA state news agency said.
There were a couple of block trades with 40,000 shares of Papastratos trading at 4,600 drachmas and 55,000 shares of Titan at 12,950 drachmas.

Losers led gainers 92 to 91 with 37 issues unchanged on 220 shares traded. Banks fell 0.50 percent, industrials eased 0.20 percent and construction increased 0.46 percent. Small-caps lost 0.44 percent. The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 561-579. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, ended down 60 drachmas at 4,220.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $7.24-$8.24. The strike price is set at $99.6 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted at 2,626-2,795 drachmas at the close. --Margarita Sotiropoulou, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
